gaps.sentence: I ___ see the sea from my bedroom window when I was little.
gaps.explanation: Verbs of perception use 'could' for past ability: could see.

gaps.sentence: We ___ have booked — the hotel had plenty of rooms left.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have' shows an unnecessary completed action: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: Applications ___ be submitted in person, not by post.
It is the only blue house on the street, so you ___ miss it.
gaps.explanation: 'You can't miss it' is an idiom meaning it is impossible not to find: can't.

gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.

gaps.sentence: She ___ have received your email — her inbox was full last week.
gaps.hint: ruled out as a past possibility
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' plus the participle rules out a past possibility: can't have received.

gaps.hint: a polite offer with would you like
gaps.explanation: 'Would you like' makes a polite offer: Would.

gaps.sentence: The ground is wet, so it ___ have rained overnight.
gaps.explanation: 'Must have' plus the participle draws a certain conclusion about the past: must have rained.
